Issue titles and environment names originate from ingested events (attacker-controllable by anyone who can send events to the project); a title containing Markdown/HTML link syntax (e.g. `[click](https://evil.example)` or an image tag) is rendered as-is in the bot's PR comment on the customer's repository, enabling content spoofing/link injection through a trusted Sentry bot account.
records.rationale: Diff introduces Markdown PR comment formatting that directly interpolates attacker-controlled strings without escaping: `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE = "* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}\n"` and `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(title=issue.title, ..., environment=self.get_environment_info(issue))`. `issue.title` comes from ingested event/group data and `get_environment_info` uses `environment.name` from the recommended event; both are inserted into GitHub/GitLab-flavored Markdown as-is, enabling Markdown/link injection/spoofing in bot-posted PR comments.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The validation error message in validate_timestamp is inverted relative to the check: it raises when a timestamp is present and age is ALSO present, but the text says "If timestamp is present, age must be absent" — and validate_age's message describes the opposite field pair, so the 422 body misdescribes which field is at fault. A client sending both fields gets a message blaming timestamp validation when the conflicting field is age (and vice versa from validate_age), misdirecting integrators debugging rejected reports; the error shape is right but the content names the wrong field.
records.rationale: The diff shows the error messages in `BrowserReportSerializer` match the actual checks. `validate_timestamp` raises only when `age` is also present (`if self.initial_data.get("age"):`) with message "If timestamp is present, age must be absent"; `validate_age` raises only when `timestamp` is also present (`if self.initial_data.get("timestamp"):`) with message "If age is present, timestamp must be absent". This is consistent (and both errors are expected when both fields are sent, as reflected in the new test `test_mixed_fields`).
